claim.quote: an upper limit on the branching ratio of B( mu+ -> e+ gamma) < 7.5 x 10^-13 (90% C.L.) is observed. The combination of this result and the limit obtained by MEG gives B( mu+ -> e+ gamma) < 3.1 x 10^-13 (90% C.L.), which is the most stringent limit to date

key_value_text.quote: The combination of this result and the limit obtained by MEG gives B($\mu^+\to e^+\gamma$) < $3.1 \times 10^{-13}$ (90% C.L.), which is the most stringent limit to date.
key_value_text.value: MEG II alone: B(mu+->e+gamma) < 7.5x10^-13 (90% C.L.); combined with MEG: < 3.1x10^-13 (90% C.L.)

name: A search for mu+ -> e+ gamma with the first dataset of the MEG II experiment

significance.quote: yielding an upper limit on the branching ratio of B($\mu^+\to e^+\gamma$) < $7.5 \times 10^{-13}$ (90% C.L.)

summary.plain: MEG II's first published result, using only its first year of data, already ties with (and combined with MEG, beats) the world's best limit on the same forbidden muon decay -- and MEG II has since collected ten times more data.
summary.technical: First-dataset (2021 physics run) MEG II result: B(mu+->e+gamma) < 7.5x10^-13 (90% C.L.) alone; combined with the final MEG limit, < 3.1x10^-13 (90% C.L.), the most stringent limit to date at publication. Dated 2024 per the arXiv v3 revision; brief refers to this as the 'MEG II 2024 limit'.

title: A search for mu+ -> e+ gamma with the first dataset of the MEG II experiment
why_it_matters: Confirms MEG II's upgraded detector is already competitive with MEG's full final dataset using a fraction of the planned exposure, validating the upgrade ahead of the much larger dataset collected in 2022-2023.
